learningObjectives: Create and access one-dimensional and multidimensional arrays.
Manipulate strings using common Java String methods.

activities.title: Array Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore indexes, elements, and the length of an array.

content.concept: A Java array stores a fixed number of values of the same type. Indexing begins at zero, and the length field gives the number of elements.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Declares a reference to an integer array.
Accesses the first element because Java arrays use zero-based indexing.
Returns the number of elements in the array.

activities.title: Index Explorer
activities.instruction: Move through the array and identify the value at each index.

content.concept: Each array element has a unique zero-based index. For an array of length n, the valid indexes range from 0 through n - 1.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: String Method Matcher
activities.instruction: Match each text operation with the appropriate Java String method.

content.concept: Common String operations include length(), substring(), contains(), equals(), and toUpperCase(). String methods return information or transformed strings without changing the original String object.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: Check whether text contains another sequence
Compare two strings for equal content

activities.title: Array Traversal Builder
activities.instruction: Build a loop that visits every element of an array.

content.concept: A standard indexed loop can traverse an array by starting at index 0 and continuing while the index is less than array.length.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.
